The image shows a leaf with a pale yellow-cream to light orange overall coloration, with the central vein visible. The leaf surface has an irregular, diffuse yellowing/orange tint, and some faint irregular patches are visible across the surface. This appears to be the underside of a leaf.

**Key observations:**
- Pale yellow-orange coloration across the leaf surface, consistent with powdery/pustule lesions on the lower leaf
- Irregular, diffuse discoloration rather than discrete circular spots with defined margins (ruling out Brown_Eye_Spot, Berry_Blotch)
- No visible dark depressed lesions (ruling out Phoma)
- No distinct pale trails/mines under epidermis (ruling out Miner)
- The overall yellowing/orange tone of the underside is characteristic of rust uredinia (spore masses erupting through stomata)

This matches Rust: "Yellow to orange powdery lesions on the lower leaf surface containing rust spores... spots mostly begin at leaf edges or tips where water collects."
